metadata.technology_specification: Electric vehicle traction motor (permanent magnet synchronous motor, PMSM)
metadata.technology_reasoning: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are the most common motor type used in electric vehicles as of 2024, due to their high efficiency, power density, and widespread adoption by major EV manufacturers worldwide.

components.reasoning: The stator with its laminated core and copper windings is a fundamental, separately manufactured component forming the stationary part of the motor.
Houses high-performance permanent magnets on the rotor core, constituting the rotating magnetic field component essential to motor operation.
Encases and protects internal motor components; typically aluminum or cast iron, procured as a separate structural part.
Critical mechanical components supporting rotor rotation; typically standard parts procured separately.
Structural parts closing the motor ends, housing the bearings and enabling mounting, standard in most motor designs.

components.component: Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling Plates)
components.reasoning: Integrated cooling components to manage motor thermal performance; commonly supplied as a subassembly with the motor or as separate cooling modules.
Transmits mechanical torque to the drivetrain; a distinct mechanical component machined and assembled within the motor.

Stator Assembly.name: Copper
Stator Assembly.reasoning: Primary conductor material for stator windings due to excellent electrical conductivity, universally used in electric motor stators.

Stator Assembly.name: Silicon
Stator Assembly.reasoning: Used as the base material in electrical steel laminations for the stator core to reduce eddy current losses; silicon steel is industry standard.

Stator Assembly.name: Iron
Stator Assembly.reasoning: Form the main magnetic core in the stator laminations; essential for electromagnetic function, widely used alloy base.

Stator Assembly.name: Epoxy resins
Stator Assembly.reasoning: Used as insulating varnish/coating on stator windings to electrically insulate wires and protect from moisture; common but alternatives exist.

Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.name: Copper
Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.reasoning: Copper used in squirrel cage rotor bars or winding due to electrical conductivity and efficiency; standard in rotor construction.

Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.name: Iron
Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.reasoning: Forms the rotor core essential for magnetic flux conduction in electromagnetic motors, universally used.

Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.name: Neodymium
Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.reasoning: Critical rare earth element for manufacturing high-strength permanent magnets in the rotor; essential for high-performance motors with permanent magnets.

Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.name: Boron
Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.reasoning: Commonly alloyed with neodymium in permanent magnets (NdFeB), improving magnetic properties; industry standard in permanent magnet manufacturing.

Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.name: Dysprosium
Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.reasoning: Added to permanent magnets to increase thermal stability and coercivity; often used but less ubiquitous than neodymium and boron.

Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.name: Epoxy resins
Rotor Assembly with Permanent Magnets.reasoning: Used as binder or coating materials in magnet assembly to protect magnets from corrosion and mechanical damage, common but optional.

Motor Housing (Enclosure).name: Aluminum
Motor Housing (Enclosure).reasoning: Commonly used for motor housing due to light weight, corrosion resistance and good thermal conductivity; industry standard material.

Motor Housing (Enclosure).name: Steel Ingots
Motor Housing (Enclosure).reasoning: Steel variants are frequently used for housings requiring increased mechanical strength, widely substituted with aluminum depending on design.

Motor Housing (Enclosure).name: Epoxy resins
Motor Housing (Enclosure).reasoning: Used in coatings or potting compounds to protect and insulate housing components; optional based on design and environment.

Bearing Assemblies.name: Steel Ingots
Bearing Assemblies.reasoning: Used to manufacture bearing races and balls due to high strength, wear resistance, and fatigue life; critical material in bearing production.

Bearing Assemblies.name: Iron
Bearing Assemblies.reasoning: Base material in bearing steel alloys providing magnetic and structural properties; commonly used but depends on alloy design.

End Bells (End Caps).name: Aluminum
End Bells (End Caps).reasoning: Widely used for end bells due to lightweight, machinability, and corrosion resistance; industry preferred.

End Bells (End Caps).name: Steel Ingots
End Bells (End Caps).reasoning: Used in some designs for mechanical strength; alternative to aluminum but heavier.

Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling.name: Aluminum
Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling.reasoning: Aluminum provides excellent thermal conductivity and corrosion resistance for cooling components; industry standard.

Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling.name: Copper
Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling.reasoning: Copper used in cooling channels or heat exchangers for superior thermal management but heavier and costlier, alternative to aluminum.

Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling.name: Epoxy resins
Cooling System (Water Jacket or Cooling.reasoning: Used in insulation and protective coatings within cooling system assemblies; not always required but common for corrosion protection.

Shaft.name: Steel Ingots
Shaft.reasoning: The shaft requires high strength and fatigue resistance, typically made from steel alloys; universally critical material.

Shaft.name: Iron
Shaft.reasoning: Constituent base metal in steel shaft alloys, essential for structural integrity though alloyed with other metals.
